source: The Scribe's voice: the ONE config for his lines and their sound (docs/next/GOAL_SCRIBE.md). Text may carry Fish S2 cues in [brackets] ([break], [long-break], [calm, warm], ...); the game shows the text with the cues removed. Edit, then run `python scripts/gen_scribe_voice.py --yes` (new text) or `--reprocess` (sound only, no API calls). A line may override `voice` (model, speed, ...) for itself. Lines with "voiced": false are shown as text only (no audio is generated): he speaks aloud rarely, on welcome, welcome back, campaign victory and a brief revive. A line may list `parts` recorded separately and spliced (the revive lines: each keeps its own opening and shares the owner-approved "Rise, once more").

lines.text: [calm, warm, gently amused] Ah. [long-break] So ye have come at last. [long-break] Enter, and mind the ink. [break] It hath been drying since before your kingdoms had names. [long-break] I am the Scribe. [break] I keep the ledger wherein every tale is set down, [break] the grand chapters, [break] and the quiet footnotes alike. [long-break] Why I keep it [break] need not trouble you. [long-break] [calm, thoughtful] Ye shall walk roads that would rather not be walked, [break] and meet things that would rather ye did not. [long-break] Yet heed one who hath read a great many endings. [long-break] The heroes who endure are seldom the strongest. [break] They are the ones who carry one another. [long-break] So each of ye, [break] guard thy companions. [break] Share thy fire, [break] thy bread, [break] thy last good counsel. [long-break] A fellowship is a page no single hand may write. [long-break] [warm, gently amused] Now then. [break] The ink is fresh, [break] and the first line is yours. [long-break] Go forth, [break] and give me something worth the writing.

[calm, warm, gently amused] Ah. [long-break] The ledger stirs once more. [break] Welcome back. [long-break] I kept your page precisely where ye left it, [break] and I confess, [break] I did not so much as correct the spelling. [long-break] The tale hath waited patiently, [break] as tales are wont to do. [long-break] Take up your places, [break] gather close, [break] and let us see what the next chapter maketh of you.

[warm, moved] And so [break] the last line is written. [long-break] I have kept this ledger a very long time, [break] and seldom do I linger over a page. [long-break] Yet I lingered over yours. [long-break] Ye came as strangers, [break] and ye leave as something rarer still: [break] a company that would not let one another fall. [long-break] [calm, warm] Rest now. [break] Your names are set in ink that doth not fade, [break] and I shall be glad to read them again.

[warm, gently amused] Well, well. [long-break] The end of the chapter, [break] and what a chapter it was. [long-break] Monsters undone, [break] debts settled, [break] and more than one plan that ought never to have worked. [long-break] I have recorded heroes who were stronger, [break] and heroes who were luckier, [break] but few so stubbornly loyal to one another. [long-break] [calm, warm] Close the book gently. [break] Tales such as yours have a way of being asked for again.

[warm, proud] Behold. [long-break] A finished tale, [break] and its heroes still standing at the end of it. [long-break] Ye would marvel how rarely that cometh to pass. [long-break] I have set down every choice, [break] every stumble, [break] every brave and foolish moment, [break] and I would not strike out a single word. [long-break] [warm, gently amused] Go, [break] and make merry, [break] my friends. [break] I shall keep your page warm.

parts.text: [calm, warm] From the final page, I call thee back.
[warm and solemn, unhurried] Rise, [break] once more.
[calm, warm] Thy name is restored to the ledger.
[warm and solemn, unhurried] Rise, [break] once more.
[calm, gently amused] Struck out, and written in anew.
[warm and solemn, unhurried] Rise, [break] once more.

lines.text: Not whilst blades are drawn, good friend. Finish thy battle, and I shall be here.
Alas, thy purse is a little light. Return when fortune hath been kinder.
Every name accounted for, and every heart still beating. How delightful.
That one is not mine to rewrite. Bind their wounds, and let them rest.
